"ORG" typically refers to an organization. It’s often used as shorthand for a group or entity that has a specific purpose, structure, or goals, such as a business, non-profit, club, or any other collective group of people working together. The term is common in various contexts, like: Non-profit organizations (NPOs): These are entities that operate for purposes other than making a profit, such as charities, advocacy groups, and foundations. Corporate organizations: For-profit companies or businesses are also referred to as organizations. Online domain: ".org" is also a top-level domain (TLD) on the internet, commonly used by non-profit organizations.
9:22 PM
A Survivor ORG (short for Survivor Online Reality Game) is an online game inspired by the popular reality TV show Survivor. In a Survivor ORG, participants compete in various challenges, form alliances, and vote each other off the game, just like on the TV show. However, these games are typically played through forums, social media platforms, or custom websites, rather than being televised. Here’s how a typical Survivor ORG works: Castaways (Players): People sign up to be part of the game, often competing in a large group at the beginning. Challenges: Players participate in physical or mental challenges that test their problem-solving, teamwork, or individual skills. These challenges are usually administered online. Tribal Divisions: Players are often divided into teams or "tribes," which will eventually merge into individual gameplay as the game progresses. Voting: After each challenge, players vote one member of their tribe off the game, usually based on performance or social dynamics. Alliance-building: Players often form alliances, trying to manipulate the social dynamics and ensure they make it to the end. Elimination: The game continues until one player remains, often with a jury of eliminated players who vote for the winner. Survivor ORGs are usually run by fans of the show, and participants may play for fun, bragging rights, or small prizes. They can vary in complexity, with some mimicking the real show closely and others having their own unique twists. Have you ever played in one, or are you considering it?
